title.pt-BR: Sistemas de Conflito da Marginal Thinking

description.en: Machine-readable conflict-system objects linking long-horizon genealogy, countries, collective perceptions, material capacity, interpretive sources, socioeconomic transmission and escalation pathways.
description.pt-BR: Objetos legíveis por máquina que conectam genealogia de longo prazo, países, percepções coletivas, capacidade material, fontes interpretativas, transmissão socioeconômica e trajetórias de escalada.

methodological_rules: Separate legal responsibility, observed facts, actor claims, analytical inference and conditional scenarios.
Treat country, government, elite coalition, institution, armed actor and population as distinct objects.
Use collective psychology only through observable evidence such as surveys, historical memory, identity, trust, threat perception and strategic narratives; do not diagnose leaders.
Store renowned thinkers, diplomats and scholars as attributed interpretive sources whose arguments can change over time; prestige is not evidence.
Do not publish a precise probability of generalized war unless an empirically defensible probability model exists.
Every material analytical proposition should preserve counterevidence, an alternative explanation and a falsifier.

genealogy.event: Ukrainian independence and formal NATO relations
Budapest Memorandum signed in connection with Ukraine's NPT accession
Bucharest Summit declaration says Ukraine and Georgia will become NATO members
NATO Lisbon declaration respects Ukraine's non-bloc status while maintaining the open-door policy
Crimea annexed by Russia and war begins in Donbas
Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
NATO Hague commitment institutionalizes a higher long-run defence-investment path
European defence spending and industrial planning remain on a higher trajectory

interpretive_sources.author: Henry Kissinger
interpretive_sources.context: Former U.S. Secretary of State; practitioner interpretation
interpretive_sources.central_proposition: Ukraine should function as a bridge between Russia and the West rather than as an outpost of either side; at that time Kissinger opposed Ukrainian NATO membership.
interpretive_sources.causal_mechanism: A balance accepted by both Russia and the West would reduce zero-sum competition over Ukraine.
assumptions: A viable neutral or bridging Ukrainian position remains institutionally and politically sustainable.
counterarguments: Ukrainian sovereign preferences and later coercion can change the feasibility and legitimacy of neutrality.
interpretive_sources.later_evidence: The 2022 full-scale invasion substantially changed the strategic environment.
interpretive_sources.position_change: By January 2023 Kissinger publicly argued that Ukrainian NATO membership had become an appropriate outcome.

interpretive_sources.author: Henry Kissinger
interpretive_sources.central_proposition: Durable international order depends on a workable relationship between power and conceptions of legitimate order.
interpretive_sources.causal_mechanism: Orders become unstable when major actors do not share sufficient rules or legitimacy while power balances also shift.
assumptions: Concepts of legitimacy and power both materially shape state behavior.
counterarguments: The framework can understate domestic politics, smaller-state agency and legal responsibility if applied too broadly.
interpretive_sources.later_evidence: Used as an interpretive lens rather than as case-specific proof.

interpretive_sources.author: M. E. Sarotte
interpretive_sources.central_proposition: Post-Cold War choices over NATO enlargement and U.S.–Russian relations were contingent and accumulated through specific decisions rather than following an inevitable path.
interpretive_sources.causal_mechanism: Institutional choices, bargaining positions and missed opportunities altered expectations and narrowed later options.
assumptions: Archival sequencing can illuminate how the security order evolved.
counterarguments: Institutional history alone cannot explain later Russian military decisions, Ukrainian domestic agency or all ideological change.
interpretive_sources.later_evidence: The 2022 invasion makes the earlier institutional sequence more consequential but does not by itself resolve causal weighting.

escalation_monitor.rule: Do not infer a probability from the composite display. Track changes by domain with source, date, direction, uncertainty and containment mechanisms.

falsifiers: A sustained political settlement with credible implementation that materially reduces Russia–NATO operational contact.
Restoration of durable arms-control and military risk-reduction mechanisms.
A sustained reversal of defence-industrial and force-planning assumptions across major European states.
Comparable longitudinal evidence showing significant declines in Russian and Ukrainian threat perceptions.
An institutional arrangement that reconciles Ukrainian sovereignty and security with a stable wider European security framework.
